about.title: Hi, I'm Buğra.
about.p1: I study Computer Science at Dokuz Eylül University. Lately my focus has been on the backend: with TypeScript, Express and PostgreSQL, I'm learning — and putting into practice — how a server handles a request and how data is stored and served. I'm building the backend of this site myself as part of that process.
about.p2: Alongside my studies, I build web projects for local businesses. Haus Pera's QR menu and Jakovs' website are two of them, and both are in use at the businesses today.

haus.title: Haus Pera Coffee — QR Menu · Nuri Buğra Demir
haus.description: A QR-code mobile menu and management panel for Haus Pera Coffee.
haus.subtitle: QR Menu
haus.lede: The digital menu in use at Haus Pera Coffee. Guests scan the code on their table to open the menu on their phone, while the business updates its products and prices from its own management panel.

guest.title: From the table to the menu
guest.s1_text: Every table has a QR card that leads to the menu; scanning it with the phone camera is all it takes.
guest.s2_title: The menu opens on the phone
guest.s2_text: It opens in the browser, with no app to install. Categories and search are on a single screen.

owner.title: Prices in the owner's hands
owner.s1_title: Prices are updated in the panel
owner.s1_text: The business signs in to its password-protected management panel and changes the price of a product. Here, the hot Latte price is being edited.
owner.s2_text: The change appears on the menu as soon as it's saved; the next guest to scan the code sees the Latte at its new price. No developer or reprinting needed.

approach.title: A simple foundation
approach.d1_text: The menu guests see and the management panel the business uses run together in a single Next.js application, so maintenance and updates happen in one place.
approach.d2_text: The entire menu is stored as a single record in the database. Since the menu is always displayed and saved as a whole, this keeps things simple and easy to manage.
approach.d3_text: Instead of being read from the database on every visit, the menu is kept ready on the server. When the business saves a change, that copy is refreshed, so guests always see the current menu.
approach.next: Next steps: dynamic QR codes and a version that multiple businesses can use.

jakovs.title: Jakovs Coffee — Website redesign · Nuri Buğra Demir
jakovs.description: Reworking Jakovs Coffee's template website around the venue's own identity.
jakovs.subtitle: Website redesign
jakovs.lede: The business had bought its website as a ready-made service through Turhost. I reworked that template site around the venue's warm atmosphere and its stone reliefs, rebuilding the visual hierarchy and the gallery layout from the ground up.

facts.focus: Colour, visual language, page layout, gallery

compare.title: From a stock template to the venue's own identity
compare.hint: Drag the line or use the arrow keys.

changes.c1_text: The template's bright lime green was replaced with deep green and warm cream tones.
changes.c2_text: A generic coffee photo gave way to the venue's own product and atmosphere photography.
changes.c3_text: The venue's emblem replaced a text-only logo, and the headline and introduction in the hero area were separated.

full.title: One flow, top to bottom
full.lede: After the hero area come the service approach, photos from the venue and the contact details. The gallery brings different corners of the venue and its products together in one consistent layout, and the page closes with a photo taken in front of the stone relief wall.

mobile.title: A single column on the phone
mobile.s1_text: The menu links collapse into a single button, and the hero area and introduction stack into one column.
mobile.s2_text: On the phone the gallery becomes a two-column grid, with the shots in front of the stone relief and the venue photos following the same layout.
